items.title: Berkshire ups Alphabet stake under Greg Abel, making it a top-3 holding
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-A, BRK-B), under new CEO Greg Abel, increased its Alphabet position, making the Google parent its third-largest U.S.-listed equity holding by market value, behind Apple (AAPL) and American Express (AXP). According to a new filing, Berkshire held roughly 106 million Alphabet shares, valued at $37.9 billion, as of the end of June. Recent reporting confirms Berkshire invested about $10 billion in Alphabet during the second quarter.

items.title: Warren Buffett's Successor, Greg Abel, Pared Down Bank of America, and Piled Into a Virtual Monopoly That's Now Berkshire's 3rd-Largest Holding
items.summary: Greg Abel's overhaul of Berkshire Hathaway's $358 billion investment portfolio continued in his second quarter at the helm.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway Makes Alphabet Its No. 3 Holding After 48M Share Buy
items.summary: According to the firm’s filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Berkshire lifted the combined GOOGL and GOOG position to about 106 million shares.

items.title: Berkshire Adds to Alphabet Stake, Buys Home Builders and Exits Constellation
items.summary: Greg Abel—CEO and top stock picker—reduced the company’s portfolio in financial shares during the second quarter.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway Boosted Alphabet, Delta Stakes in 2nd Quarter, Sold Bank of America
items.summary: Berkshire’s Alphabet stake—consisting of the search giant’s voting and nonvoting shares—rose about 80% in the quarter to 106 million shares, reflecting a purchase directly from Alphabet in June and open-market buys, based on a 13-F report with the Securities and Exchange Commission late Friday.  Berkshire was a seller of part of its sizable stake in  Bank of America  cutting it by 30 million shares to 483 million shares now worth about $31 billion.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway expands Alphabet stake and trims bank exposure in Q2
items.summary: Investing.com -- Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKb) aggressively expanded its stake in Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) during the second quarter, signaling a deepening conviction in the technology giant’s strategic trajectory. According to the Omaha-based conglomerate’s latest 13F filing, the firm added tens of millions of shares across both share classes, lifting its Class C holdings to over 27 million while bolstering its Class A position to nearly 79 million shares. items.title: Seth Klarman Just Quietly Bought a Piece of Bill Ackman’s Firm
items.summary: Seth Klarman built his reputation by staying quiet and staying out of the spotlight, so when the most reclusive value investor of his generation puts money into Bill Ackman's publicly listed firm, the question worth asking is what he sees that most investors are missing.

items.title: This ETF Copies Buffett’s Portfolio and Pays You Monthly. Why Buffett Would Never.
items.summary: A new ETF mirrors Warren Buffett's stock picks and mails you a check every month, doing everything Buffett has famously refused to do for seven decades. The gap between admiring his portfolio and investing the way he actually invests turns out to be enormous.
